name: accordion
description: UIDS accordion component contract, preserving the verified 4.x rendering and documenting the proposed Figma representation.

figma.note: BUILT (Phase 3). ICON CORRECTED 2026-08-17. The SET models a single 'Accordion Item' — Color (Default, White) x State (Closed, Open) = 2x2 = 4 variants — not the multi-item role=tablist wrapper, which has no BEM modifier of its own and whose only real content axis (items, arbitrary length) cannot be a Figma variant. The wrapper is an auto-layout stacking frame holding N instances.
axisRationale: Single-item modelling mirrors the Logo-nests-in-Brand-Bar and Form-Item-nests-in-Form-Fieldset precedent: the wrapper stacks instances rather than being a variant grid itself.
multiselectable is NOT an axis (Button borderless/full precedent) — it has zero visual expression; it is code-only, via native <details name> behaviour.

The icon is a real TEXT node: font 'Font Awesome 6 Free' style 'Solid', character U+F077 (fa-chevron-up), fontSize 19.2, black fill, in a 22.4x22.4 box bound to accordion/icon/size. DO NOT convert it back to a vector — the webfont glyph is exact and the production DOM has no <path> to copy from.
Closed is the SAME glyph at rotation 180, matching the CSS, which rotates one .fa-chevron-up rather than swapping to chevron-down. A 180-degree rotation of a square box is layout-neutral.

The icon sits BEFORE the heading text, because Accordion.vue renders <i class='fas fa-chevron-up'> before {{ item.title }} inside a flex h2 — and the CSS margin -4.8px 11.2px 0 0 is a RIGHT margin, which only makes sense for an icon on the left.

The heading frame is primaryAxisAlignItems MIN with itemSpacing bound to accordion/icon/gap (measured 11.2 against the live component's 11.19). It must not be SPACE_BETWEEN — that fakes icon-on-the-right and makes itemSpacing inert.
deliberateOmissions: The icon's own fontSize (19.2) stays a raw value: no token exists for it — the same untokenized-icon gap already recorded for menu's active-indicator colour.
figma.precedent: Logo in Brand Bar / Form Item in Form Fieldset (single-item modelling).

options.name: items
options.description: Keys per item: title, content, id, open. `id` is optional — Accordion.vue builds an itemIds list and falls back to a generated id when an item omits one, so ids only need supplying when a caller wants stable anchors. `open` sets the item's initial expanded state; more than one may be open at a time only when multiselectable is set. Required, with no default: the component renders nothing without it. Added 2026-08-20 to close the long-standing check-contracts warning that this Vue prop was unclaimed by any contract option — the schema already supported array/object option types.

code.notes: Vue marks it required:true with type:Array and no default.

figma.notes: Content, not a variant axis: the number of entries drives how many rows/tabs/crumbs are drawn, which Figma expresses by duplicating the child instance rather than by a variant property.

options.name: multiselectable
options.description: Controls whether multiple items can be open at once. Also drives aria-multiselectable on the wrapper and toggles the native <details name> exclusive-group attribute on every item (see behavior) — the ONLY part of this prop with any visible effect; its own CSS modifier is dead (see claims).

code.notes: Also adds the class 'accordion--multi' (Accordion.vue:38), which has zero corresponding CSS in either repo — see claims/knownIssues.

figma.notes: Deliberately NOT a variant axis — no CSS/visual difference exists between true/false (Button borderless/full precedent). The real effect is a native HTML attribute with no visual analog for a designer to see in Figma.

options.name: label_color
options.description: Colorway. '' (the real Vue default; Storybook's own control labels it 'Gray' since the rendered default summary background is gray/100) renders the base gray label bar with a new-primitive hover; 'white' renders a white label bar with a gray/100 hover — the two colorways' label/hover values are an inverted pair (see tier3Tokens).

code.notes: Gated by plain JS truthiness on the raw prop string (Accordion.vue:39, 'accordion--white': props.label_color) — NOT a strict === 'white' check. The Vue prop itself has no validator restricting it to an enum (String, default '', required: false), so any non-empty string would also trigger the white styling today, though only '' and 'white' are documented/exercised in Storybook. See openQuestions.

slots.name: items
slots.description: NOT a Vue <slot> — Accordion.vue has zero <slot> elements; this is a required Array prop (Accordion.vue:18-21), each entry an object { id, title, content, open? }, that the template v-fors over to produce the repeated accordion markup. Documented here because it plays the role a slot/content-prop would in Headline/Button, and the contract schema's options[].type enum (boolean/string/enum/number) has no way to represent an array — see openQuestions.
slots.behavior:
Each item renders

{{ item.title }}

. item.content is rendered via v-html (raw HTML, unescaped — content authors are trusted). The wrapper's aria-owns is every item.id joined with a space; item.open sets the native
attribute directly with no JS involvement for initial state.

figma.notes: Model as N repeated 'Accordion Item' component instances inside a stacking frame, not as a property on one instance — see figmaProposal.

behavior: multiselectable=false (default) sets name="accordion-collection" on every <details> (Accordion.vue:59) — the native browser exclusive-accordion-group attribute; only one item can be open at a time, entirely via HTML, with no CSS or JS enforcement. multiselectable=true sets name=null so items open independently. This is a real behavioral difference despite its CSS-facing class ('accordion--multi') being completely unstyled — see claims.

Accordion.vue hardcodes <h2> for every item's heading (Accordion.vue:66) with no prop to change it — the CSS's own `.accordion__heading :is(h2, h3, h4, h5, h6)` selector (accordion.scss:53) can therefore never render its h3-h6 branches from this Vue component or in Storybook. SiteNow's downstream accordion-item.html.twig, however, parameterizes accordion_h_size (default h2, overridable per item — see paragraph--accordion-item--default.html.twig:43) and DOES render h3-h6 in production — so the selector is fully live there. See claims (scoped 'unreachable from Vue') and openQuestions (should Accordion.vue gain a matching heading-level prop?).

accordion.js (applyAccordion, wired onMounted) manages hash-based deep-linking: a click on <summary> sets a transient data-accordion-clicked attribute BEFORE the native 'toggle' event fires (click fires first), so the toggle handler can tell a user click from a programmatic one; opening replaces the URL hash with '#' + the summary's id, closing clears it. A popstate listener plus an initial-load check both call focusAccordionItemByHash(), which finds the element by id and calls .click() to open it — pure behavior, touches no tokenizable CSS.
label_color gates '.accordion--white' via plain JS truthiness on the raw prop string (Accordion.vue:39), not a strict === 'white' comparison — see the label_color option's code.notes.

The wrapper is role="tablist" with aria-multiselectable and aria-owns (every item id, joined); each <details> is role="none" and each <summary> is role="tab" — a custom repurposing of the tablist/tab ARIA roles onto native <details>/<summary> elements. Unchanged by this migration, noted for context only.

Production styling depends on cross-repo overrides this repo's SCSS doesn't capture: uids_base's theme accordion.scss sets `.accordion .accordion__heading { color: variables.$secondary }` (brandChannel-eligible; accordion.scss itself declares no heading text color), and uiowa_paragraphs_accordion.scss re-themes in-content links inside .accordion__content using Button's own bttn--primary/bttn--secondary/bttn--focus mixins. See openQuestions.
knownIssues: Accordion.vue is exported from its own local index.ts but is NOT re-exported from src/components/index.ts, the package barrel every other migrated component uses (alert/banner/brand-bar/brand-footer/button/card/cta/headline/logo/menu). Storybook imports Accordion.vue directly by relative path, so this doesn't block Storybook or this migration, but Accordion currently has no established registeredName/barrelExport identity at all — no `const name = 'uids-accordion'` exists either (unlike Button's and Headline's own dead-but-present constants) — this migration mints that identity fresh rather than inheriting one.

AccordionDocs.mdx's 'Usage' section (lines 11-13) tells consumers to add logo.css and brand-bar.css to their project — copy-pasted from Brand Bar/Logo's own docs and never updated. Accordion actually depends on _background.scss (imported directly in Accordion.vue:5), which the docs don't mention at all.
.accordion--multi is a no-op CSS modifier (see claims) — do not model it in Figma/tokens. The multiselectable prop's real effect is the native <details name> attribute (see behavior), not this class.
.accordion--white's border-color override is redundant CSS, byte-identical to the base value (see claims) — modeled as one shared accordion/border/color token, not a per-colorway pair.

uids_base's `.accordion .accordion__heading button.border` rule (that repo's accordion.scss:29-31, marked with its own '@todo remove when .../issues/714') targets a <button> element that exists in neither repo's current markup — dead/unreachable, downstream-owned; flagged for the ticket owner rather than modeled here (see claims).

geometryNotTokenized.transition-timing: --trans-time: 0.2s (accordion.scss:7), consumed by the icon's `transition: all var(--trans-time) ease-in-out` (line 39) and `transition-property: transform, background-color` (line 47). Left untokenized, matching Button's own precedent (button.json geometryNotTokenized.focus-bar-motion: '...transition transform 0.3s ease-in-out. Only its color and height are tokenized.') — motion durations are treated as rendering mechanics, not identity-bearing values, across the components migrated so far.
geometryNotTokenized.icon-vertical-offset: margin: -0.3rem .7rem 0 0 (accordion.scss:45) — only the .7rem (accordion/icon/gap) is tokenized; the -0.3rem top offset is a one-off optical-centering hack tied to this specific chevron glyph's line-box, not a portable design decision.
geometryNotTokenized.chevron-rotation: Closed state: rotate(-180deg) translate(0px, -0.1em) (accordion.scss:49); open state ([open] summary i, svg): rotate(0deg) translate(0px, 0.1em) (accordion.scss:17). Presentation constants tied to the specific chevron-up glyph and the native <details> toggle — Brand Bar geometryNotTokenized precedent (a real design decision that isn't naturally a bindable token; a Figma Open/Closed variant reproduces it by hand).
geometryNotTokenized.icon-border-radius: border-radius: 50% (accordion.scss:46) — a shape constant (perfect circle), not identity-bearing.
geometryNotTokenized.heading-focus-outline: outline: 2px auto -webkit-focus-ring-color (accordion.scss:66) — the native browser default focus ring, never overridden; same class of finding as Button's a11y notes (focus indicated by browser default).
geometryNotTokenized.border-width: 1px solid on both .accordion__item (line 93, full border) and .accordion__content's border-top (line 73) — width and style stay raw geometry; only the color is tokenized (accordion/border/color), matching Button's own border treatment (button.json geometryNotTokenized.border).
geometryNotTokenized.content-last-child-margin: p:last-child { margin-bottom: 0px; } (accordion.scss:76) inside .accordion__content — a one-off reset, not a design value.
geometryNotTokenized.table-nested-font-size-reset: table ul li, table ol li, table p { font-size: inherit; } (accordion.scss:85-88) — resets the tokenized 1.3rem list/paragraph size back to inherit specifically for lists/paragraphs nested inside a <table> within accordion content. The value is the CSS keyword inherit, not a design value, so nothing to tokenize; kept as-shipped.
